title: Independence and Ingathering
intro: Israel declares independence, wins its first war and doubles its population in three years as Jews pour in from Europe and the Arab world.
tp: David Ben-Gurion declares independence and becomes prime minister of the provisional government. Five Arab armies attack on May 15.
Five Arab armies invade the day after independence. By the armistices of 1949 Israel holds more land than the partition plan gave it.
Armistice agreements with Egypt (Feb 24), Lebanon (Mar 23), Jordan (Apr 3) and Syria (Jul 20) end the War of Independence. Israel holds more land than the partition plan gave it.
In flights that began in 1949, the Yemenite Jewish airlift brings nearly 49,000 Jews from Yemen and Aden to Israel by September 1950.
Airlifts bring about 120,000 Jews from Iraq to Israel.
Every Jew has the right to immigrate to Israel and take citizenship.
Israel and West Germany sign in Luxembourg. Menachem Begin leads a violent protest outside the Knesset in January over the talks.
Israeli agents recruit Egyptian Jews for failed bombings in Egypt. Two are executed, and Defense Minister Pinhas Lavon resigns, with Ben-Gurion returning to the post.
also: The Israel Defense Forces are formed from the Haganah and other groups.
Chaim Weizmann is elected the first president.
Territory: Jordan annexes Judea and Samaria and East Jerusalem.
Jews arrive from Arab countries and Iran and reshape Israeli society.
King Abdullah of Jordan is assassinated in Jerusalem.
Egypt bars Israeli shipping from the Suez Canal.
The Free Officers coup in Egypt brings Nasser to power.
Yad Vashem is founded by law to remember the Holocaust.
The Qibya raid draws sharp international criticism.
Ben-Gurion resigns and moves to Sde Boker.
Moshe Sharett becomes prime minister while Ben-Gurion rests at Sde Boker.
Gunmen kill 11 Israelis on a bus at Scorpion Pass.
Yehuda Amichai publishes his first poems, Now and in Other Days.
Egypt announces an arms deal with Czechoslovakia.

title: Sinai and the Years Between
intro: The Sinai Campaign opens a decade of quiet borders. Israel builds its water carrier and its institutions, tries Eichmann and makes peace with Germany.
tp: After Egypt nationalizes the Suez Canal, Israel, Britain and France plan the attack in secret at Sèvres. Israel takes Sinai in days. The United States and the Soviet Union force a withdrawal, completed in March 1957.
Israeli agents seize Adolf Eichmann in Argentina in 1960. He is tried in Jerusalem in 1961 and executed in 1962, the only death sentence Israel has carried out in a civil court.
A secret Mossad operation brings about 100,000 Jews from Morocco to Israel.
Levi Eshkol becomes prime minister as the founding generation begins to hand over power.
It brings water from the Sea of Galilee to the farms and towns of the south.
Twenty years after the Holocaust, the two countries exchange ambassadors.
S. Y. Agnon is the first Hebrew writer to receive the prize for literature.
also: Border police kill 48 Arab citizens at Kafr Qasim.
A UN emergency force deploys in Sinai and Gaza.
Thousands of Jews leave Egypt after the Sinai War.
Territory: Israel completes its withdrawal from Sinai and Gaza.
France agrees to help build the Dimona reactor.
Egypt and Syria merge into the United Arab Republic.
The Hebrew University opens its new campus at Givat Ram in Jerusalem.
Israel begins building the Dimona reactor.
A coup in Iraq and a crisis in Lebanon alarm Israel’s neighbors and its allies.
Riots break out in Haifa’s Wadi Salib over discrimination against Jews from North Africa.
Marc Chagall’s windows are dedicated at the Hadassah synagogue in Jerusalem.
Pope Paul VI makes the first papal visit to the Holy Land in modern times.
The Arab League founds the PLO.
Ephraim Kishon’s film Sallah Shabati is the first Israeli film nominated for an Academy Award.
Israeli spy Eli Cohen is hanged in Damascus.
The Israel Museum opens in Jerusalem, with the Shrine of the Book.
Military rule over Arab citizens of Israel ends.

title: The Six-Day War and Yom Kippur
intro: In six days Israel reunites Jerusalem and triples its territory. The War of Attrition, terror abroad and the shock of Yom Kippur follow.
tp: Israel takes Judea and Samaria, Gaza, Sinai, the Golan Heights and East Jerusalem. Jerusalem is united under Israeli control.
Israeli forces take the Old City, the Western Wall and the rest of Judea and Samaria, Sinai, Gaza and the Golan Heights.
Egypt shells Israeli positions along the Suez Canal and Israel answers with air raids deep in Egypt. The fighting is heaviest from March 1969 and a ceasefire takes hold on August 7, 1970.
The UN Security Council calls for Israeli withdrawal from territories and for peace and secure borders. Arab leaders had already declared three refusals at Khartoum.
She follows Levi Eshkol, who died in office on February 26. She resigns in April 1974 after the Yom Kippur War.
Palestinian terrorists kill 11 Israeli athletes and coaches at the Olympic Games.
Egypt and Syria attack on the holiest day of the year and Israel repels them. Ceasefires take hold on October 22 and 25.
Commandos fly to Uganda and rescue the hostages of a hijacked Air France plane. Yoni Netanyahu is killed leading the raid.
also: Egypt closes the Straits of Tiran to Israeli shipping.
Moshe Dayan becomes defense minister days before the Six-Day War.
Israeli aircraft and torpedo boats attack the American ship USS Liberty.
Territory: Israel extends its law and administration to East Jerusalem.
Summit: Arab leaders meet at Khartoum and refuse peace, recognition and negotiation with Israel.
Settlers return to Kfar Etzion, the first Israeli settlement after the war.
Egyptian missiles sink the Israeli destroyer Eilat.
Israeli forces fight the PLO at Karameh in Jordan.
A Passover stay in Hebron leads to the founding of Kiryat Arba.
Palestinian gunmen hijack an El Al plane to Algiers.
Israeli commandos raid Beirut airport after an attack on an El Al plane in Athens.
A fire damages the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem.
A bomb on a Swissair plane kills 47 after takeoff from Zurich.
Massacre at Lod Airport. Three Japanese gunmen working for a Palestinian group kill 26 people, most of them Puerto Rican pilgrims.
Territory: Israel and Egypt sign the first Sinai disengagement agreement.
Gunmen kill 18 people in Kiryat Shmona.
Massacre at Ma’alot. Gunmen seize a school in the north. Twenty-two schoolchildren are among the dead.
Territory: Israel and Syria sign a disengagement agreement on the Golan Heights.
Yitzhak Rabin becomes prime minister for the first time.
A bomb in Jerusalem’s Zion Square kills 15.
Territory: the second Sinai agreement returns the Abu Rudeis oil fields and the passes.

title: Upheaval, Peace and Intifada
intro: Begin’s victory ends Labor rule and leads to peace with Egypt. The Lebanon War, the First Intifada and the great Soviet aliyah follow.
tp: Likud wins the May 17 election and Menachem Begin becomes prime minister, ending three decades of Labor rule.
The Egyptian president addresses the Knesset and opens the way to peace.
The Camp David summit of September 1978 leads to the first peace treaty with an Arab state. Israel completes its return of Sinai on April 25, 1982.
Jets strike Iraq’s nuclear reactor near Baghdad before it can go into operation.
Israel invades to drive out the PLO, which leaves Beirut in August. Israel stays in southern Lebanon until 2000.
Thousands of Ethiopian Jews are brought to Israel by way of Sudan.
A Palestinian uprising begins in Gaza and spreads to Judea and Samaria. It lasts until 1993.
The Soviet Union opens its gates.
A mass aliyah begins that brings about a million Jews to Israel within a decade.
Scud missiles in the Gulf War.
Iraq fires about 40 missiles at Israeli cities. Israel does not respond.
also: Zubin Mehta becomes music director of the Israel Philharmonic.
The Coastal Road massacre. Gunmen land from the sea, hijack a bus and kill 38 civilians, 13 of them children.
Israel wins the Eurovision Song Contest.
Summit: Begin and Sadat meet with President Carter at Camp David.
Menachem Begin shares the Nobel Peace Prize with Anwar Sadat.
Terrorists land by sea and attack Nahariya.
Terrorists seize the nursery at Kibbutz Misgav Am.
Gunmen kill six yeshiva students in Hebron.
Territory: The Knesset passes the Jerusalem Law, which declares the united city the capital of Israel.
Anwar Sadat is assassinated in Cairo.
Territory: the Knesset applies Israeli law to the Golan Heights.
Israel leaves Sinai. The last of the peninsula returns to Egypt under the peace treaty, and the town of Yamit is evacuated.
An attack on the Israeli ambassador in London sparks the Lebanon War.
Lebanese militias massacre Palestinians at Sabra and Shatila.
A car bomb destroys the Israeli headquarters in Tyre.
The Kahan Commission. It finds Ariel Sharon indirectly responsible for Sabra and Shatila, and he leaves the Defense Ministry.
Ofra Haza places second at the Eurovision Song Contest.
Israel and Lebanon sign an agreement that is canceled in 1984.
In the Bus 300 affair, two hijackers die in custody.
Security forces arrest the Jewish Underground.
Shimon Peres becomes prime minister in a rotation with Shamir.
Israel frees 1,150 prisoners for three captured soldiers.
Territory: Israel pulls back to a security zone in southern Lebanon.
The economic stabilization plan. The unity government brings inflation of over 400 percent down within a year.
Israeli jets bomb PLO headquarters in Tunis.
An Egyptian policeman kills seven Israeli tourists at Ras Burqa.
Hijackers seize the cruise ship Achille Lauro.
Gunmen attack El Al counters at Rome and Vienna airports.
Yaacov Agam’s Fire and Water Fountain is installed in Dizengoff Square.
Gunmen kill 22 worshippers at the Neve Shalom synagogue in Istanbul.
Navigator Ron Arad is captured in Lebanon.
Shamir returns as prime minister in the rotation.
Summit: Peres and King Hussein agree to the London Agreement.
A hang glider attack from Lebanon kills six soldiers.
Terrorists hijack a bus near Dimona and three civilians die.
Abu Jihad is killed in Tunis.
Territory: Jordan renounces its claim to Judea and Samaria.
The PLO declares a state at its Algiers meeting.
The United States opens a dialogue with the PLO.
Territory: Israel returns Taba to Egypt after international arbitration.
Shamir proposes elections in Judea and Samaria and Gaza.
A terrorist drives Bus 405 into a ravine and 16 die.
Gunmen kill nine Israeli tourists on a bus in Egypt.
A. B. Yehoshua publishes Mr. Mani.
Police kill 17 Palestinians in riots on the Temple Mount.
Operation Solomon. About 14,000 Ethiopian Jews are flown to Israel in 36 hours.
Summit: the Madrid Peace Conference opens the first direct talks.
The UN repeals its Zionism is racism resolution.
Israel and China establish diplomatic relations.
Israel and India establish full diplomatic relations.
A bomb destroys the Israeli embassy in Buenos Aires and 29 die.
Etgar Keret publishes his first stories, Pipelines.
Yitzhak Rabin becomes prime minister for the second time.
Israel deports 415 Hamas activists to Lebanon.

title: Oslo and the Second Intifada
intro: The Oslo Accords and peace with Jordan raise hopes. Rabin is murdered, the Camp David talks fail and the Second Intifada brings suicide bombings to Israel’s cities.
tp: Israel and the PLO sign the Declaration of Principles on the White House lawn. The Palestinian Authority is created.
Rabin and King Hussein sign the treaty and normalize relations.
A Jewish extremist shoots the prime minister after a peace rally in Tel Aviv. Shimon Peres takes over the same day.
Suicide bombers kill 45 people on Jerusalem buses in February and March.
Israel leaves the security zone in southern Lebanon after 18 years.
After the Camp David summit fails, a wave of suicide bombings and fighting lasts until 2005.
He beats Ehud Barak in the special election of February 6. He withdraws from Gaza in 2005, and a stroke ends his career in January 2006.
A suicide bomber kills 30 people at a Passover seder in Netanya.
also: Israel and the Vatican sign the Fundamental Agreement.
Baruch Goldstein kills 29 worshippers in Hebron.
A suicide bomber kills eight on a bus in Afula.
Territory: Israel withdraws from the Gaza Strip and Jericho.
A bomb at the AMIA center in Buenos Aires kills 85.
A suicide bomber kills 22 on a bus on Dizengoff Street.
Three share the Nobel Peace Prize. Yitzhak Rabin, Shimon Peres and Yasser Arafat are honored for the Oslo Accords.
Two bombs at Beit Lid kill mostly soldiers.
Territory: the Oslo II agreement divides Judea and Samaria into Areas A, B and C.
A suicide bomber kills 13 at the Dizengoff Center.
Summit: leaders meet at Sharm el-Sheikh against terrorism.
Operation Grapes of Wrath against Hezbollah.
Benjamin Netanyahu becomes prime minister after beating Shimon Peres in the May 29 election.
Riots follow the opening of the Western Wall Tunnel exit.
Territory: Israel withdraws from most of Hebron under the Hebron Protocol.
Two helicopters collide and 73 soldiers die.
Suicide bombers kill 16 at the Mahane Yehuda market.
Three suicide bombers kill five on Ben Yehuda Street.
Twelve naval commandos die in an ambush in Lebanon.
A failed Mossad plot against Khaled Mashal in Amman.
Dana International wins the Eurovision Song Contest.
Summit: Netanyahu and Arafat sign the Wye River Memorandum.
Daniel Barenboim and Edward Said found the West-Eastern Divan Orchestra.
Ehud Barak becomes prime minister after beating Netanyahu on May 17.
Summit: Israel and Syria open talks at Shepherdstown.
Summit: Barak and Arafat meet at Camp David and fail to agree.
The Dolphinarium bombing. A suicide bomber kills 21 people outside a Tel Aviv discotheque, most of them teenagers.
Menashe Kadishman’s Fallen Leaves opens at the Jewish Museum Berlin.
The Sbarro bombing. A suicide bomber kills 15 people, seven of them children, in a Jerusalem pizzeria.
Operation Defensive Shield in Judea and Samaria.
A truck bomb at the Djerba synagogue kills 21.
Israel begins building a security barrier.
Daniel Kahneman wins the Nobel Prize in Economics.
Amos Oz publishes A Tale of Love and Darkness.
Attacks at a hotel in Mombasa, Kenya, kill 13.
Summit: Sharon and Abbas meet President Bush at Aqaba.
Two Technion chemists win the Nobel Prize. Aaron Ciechanover and Avram Hershko are honored for work on how cells break down proteins.
Bombs at Taba and Ras Shitan in Sinai kill 34.

title: Disengagement and the Gaza Wars
intro: Israel leaves Gaza, Hamas takes it over and three wars follow. Lebanon flares in 2006, and Gilad Shalit comes home after five years.
tp: Israel removes all its soldiers and communities from the Strip.
It follows a cross-border Hezbollah attack and ends with a UN ceasefire.
Hamas drives out the Palestinian Authority after winning elections in January 2006.
A three-week war in Gaza follows years of rocket fire on southern Israel.
Hundreds of thousands march over housing and the cost of living.
Hamas frees the soldier after five years in captivity in exchange for 1,027 prisoners.
A 50-day war with Hamas follows rocket fire and the murder of three Israeli teenagers.
also: Summit: Sharon and Mahmoud Abbas meet at Sharm el-Sheikh.
Robert Aumann wins the Nobel Prize in Economics for his work on game theory.
Hamas wins the Palestinian legislative elections.
Ehud Olmert becomes prime minister after Kadima wins on March 28.
Summit: the Annapolis Conference relaunches talks.
Waltz with Bashir wins the Golden Globe for best foreign film.
Gunmen attack the Chabad House in Mumbai.
Benjamin Netanyahu returns as prime minister.
Ada Yonath wins the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
Israeli commandos board the Gaza flotilla and nine die.
Summit: direct talks reopen in Washington.
Terrorists murder five members of the Fogel family in Itamar.
Iron Dome intercepts its first rocket from Gaza.
Dan Shechtman wins the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the discovery of quasicrystals.
Attacks near Eilat kill eight Israelis.
A gunman kills four at a Jewish school in Toulouse.
A bomb in Burgas, Bulgaria, kills five Israeli tourists.
Operation Pillar of Defense in Gaza.
The UN General Assembly upgrades the Palestinian delegation.
The singer Arik Einstein dies and crowds gather in Tel Aviv to mourn him.
Summit: direct talks resume in Washington.
The United States-led peace talks end.
A gunman kills four at the Jewish Museum in Brussels.
Three Israeli teenagers are kidnapped and murdered.
Two attackers kill five at a synagogue in Har Nof.

title: Abraham Accords to October 7
intro: The embassy moves to Jerusalem and the Abraham Accords bring peace with Gulf states. Five elections and the judicial protests divide Israel, and Hamas attacks on October 7.
tp: Iran and the world powers sign an agreement that Israel opposes. Netanyahu had argued against it before Congress in March.
The United States moves its embassy to Jerusalem.
It follows the 2017 recognition of Jerusalem as Israel’s capital.
The United Arab Emirates and Bahrain sign at the White House and normalize relations with Israel. Morocco and Sudan follow.
An 11-day war with Hamas sets off riots in mixed Arab and Jewish cities.
A broad coalition ends Netanyahu’s 12 years in office.
Mass demonstrations over the government’s proposed judicial changes divide the country.
About 1,200 people are killed and about 250 are taken hostage. Israel launches the war in Gaza, Operation Swords of Iron.
also: Terrorists kill four at a Paris kosher supermarket.
A wave of stabbings and car attacks begins.
Two gunmen kill four at the Sarona Market.
UN Security Council Resolution 2334 criticizes Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria.
The United States recognizes Jerusalem as Israel’s capital.
David Grossman wins the Man Booker International Prize.
A shooting on the Temple Mount sparks a crisis.
The Great March of Return begins at the Gaza fence.
The Nation-State Law defines Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people.
Netta wins the Eurovision Song Contest.
Territory: the United States recognizes Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights.
Election: Likud and Blue and White tie at 35.
Tel Aviv hosts the Eurovision Song Contest.
Election: Blue and White 33 seats, Likud 32.
Operation Black Belt targets Islamic Jihad in Gaza.
Netanyahu and Benny Gantz form a unity government.
Benjamin Netanyahu returns as prime minister after the November 1 election.

title: The Seven-Front War
intro: The day after the massacre, Israel is at war on seven fronts: Gaza, Lebanon, Syria, Judea and Samaria, Yemen, Iraq and Iran. Hezbollah’s leaders fall, Assad’s regime collapses, and a ceasefire brings the living hostages home.
tp: Hezbollah fires on the north the day after the massacre, and some 60,000 Israelis leave their homes.
Iran fires missiles and drones at Israel.
About 320 missiles and drones are launched. Israel says 99 percent are intercepted.
Fighting that began on October 8, 2023 ends.
The Assad regime falls in Syria.
Israel moves to secure its Golan border.
Israel strikes Iran’s nuclear and missile sites, and the United States joins in.
A ceasefire takes effect under a United States plan. The surviving hostages are released on October 13.
also: The Houthis in Yemen launch their first missiles toward Israel.
A truce frees 105 hostages in exchange for Palestinian prisoners.
A Hezbollah rocket kills 12 children on a football field in Majdal Shams.
Exploding pagers and radios wound thousands of Hezbollah members.
Israel kills Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah in Beirut.
Israeli soldiers kill Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar in Rafah.
A Gaza ceasefire begins. It ends March 18.
A Flydubai flight to Tel Aviv is attacked in the cockpit. Passengers and the Indian captain foil the hijacking.
